Step 1

You buy, we hold

$100 is authorized on PayPal. It is reserved for the vendor, but not paid yet.

Step 2

AI reads the contract

It pulls out the promises: uptime, speed and what happens if they are broken.

Step 3

We watch the service

Live monitoring catches the outage. Uptime hits 97%, not the promised 99.9%.

Step 4

Math decides, not AI

A rules engine works out the credit. Same input, same answer, every time.

Step 5

A human stays in control

Big payouts wait for approval. Nothing moves on its own.

Step 6

Everyone gets what is fair

$75 goes to the vendor. $25 comes back to you. Every dollar has a receipt.

Features

Everything between a promise and a payment.

AI reads the contract

Upload an SLA PDF. Uptime, latency and credit rules come out as structured data.

Live monitoring

Uptime and latency stream in, and every breach is flagged against the promise.

Rules engine, not an LLM

Credits come from deterministic math that you can test and trust.

Policy gate

Auto-approve, ask a human, or block. Risky payouts never move alone.

PayPal settlement

Authorize first, then capture only what the vendor actually earned.

Evidence audit trail

Every dollar links to its clause, metric, calculation, reviewer and transaction.

How it works

Six steps, from contract to cash.

1

Buy

The buyer agent buys a service with an SLA. The payment is authorized on PayPal, not captured.

2

Understand

AI extracts the measurable promises from the SLA PDF as structured data.

3

Monitor

Uptime, latency and incident data stream in and are checked against the contract.

4

Settle

The rules engine calculates the outcome. Met means full capture, breached means partial.

5

Policy gate

Act automatically, ask a human for approval, or block the payment.

6

Audit

Every amount links to its clause, metric, calculation, reviewer and PayPal transaction ID.
